name: Jason
description: Brother of Onias the high priest; bought the high priesthood from Antiochus Epiphanes and brought Jerusalem to Greek fashions, building a place of exercise and training youth after the heathen manner; undermined in turn by Menelaus and driven out, he later attacked the city, slew his own countrymen, and died in exile after being driven from land to land

points: After the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus called Epiphanes took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest. This is his own blood brother. Not only does Onias have to deal with Simon of the tribe of Benjamin; his own blood brother is trying to take the priesthood from him. Put yourself in his sandals: his good friend Simon turned on him, and now his brother.

Such was the height of Greek fashions, an increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch and no high priest. Sports is a Greek fashion: the coliseums are shaped the same way as the football stadiums today, and in them we were the entertainment.

When he had gotten the rule into his hand, he forthwith brought his own nation to the Greekish fashion; he put down the governments which were according to the law and brought up new customs against the law; he built gladly a place of exercise, brought the chief young men under his subjection, and made them wear a hat: the hat of Hermes, shown in class alongside the discus statue. Such was the height of Greek fashions and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest. Though he had the rule, the writer says he is not the true high priest.

Then Jason, who had undermined his own brother, being undermined by another, was compelled to flee into the country of the Ammonites. Now the high priest is of the tribe of Benjamin. You cannot make this stuff up.

When there was gone forth a false rumour, as though Antiochus had been dead, Jason took at the least a thousand men and suddenly made an assault upon the city, and Menelaus fled into the castle. Now Menelaus is running from his one-time friend Jason, whose priesthood he took. But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, because he despised his own people.

source.name: TIPNR, Translators Individualised Proper Names with all References, by Tyndale House Cambridge, STEPBible.org

cases.name: Jason the high priest
cases.charge: Buying the priesthood; setting up a Greek gymnasium; drawing his countrymen to heathen customs
cases.preview: When Antiochus called Epiphanes took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias worked underhand for the priesthood, promising the king three hundred and threescore talents of silver and more besides…
